name: target_prepare_ready_for_offer
currentOutcome: The endpoint emits target preparation statuses, but the V2 dialog creates its offer immediately.
v2Gate: Create an offer only after the exact target/provider is ready.

name: offer_answer_ice
currentOutcome: The gateway relays bounded ordered signalling and the helper owns direct WebRTC.
v2Gate: Fence directional sequences and negotiation generation without persisting SDP or ICE.

name: duplicate_signal
currentOutcome: The current registry rejects duplicate or lower agent session sequences.
v2Gate: Deduplicate by direction, generation and message ID.

name: reordered_signal
currentOutcome: The current registry is monotonic rather than contiguous.
v2Gate: Specify explicit out-of-order handling per negotiation generation.

name: browser_reconnect
currentOutcome: The browser peer can restart on a gateway reconnect, but has no durable cursor/resume authority.
v2Gate: Authorize operator-bound cursor resume or require renegotiation.

name: agent_gateway_reconnect
currentOutcome: Same-process replacement replays open and resets agent sequence fencing.
v2Gate: Fresh presence epoch and edge-route registration are required after loss.

name: first_frame_timeout
currentOutcome: The JavaScript asset can report a first frame, while the current dialog does not use it as the connected gate.
v2Gate: A current-peer first frame is required before Connected.

name: data_channel_missing
currentOutcome: The JavaScript asset reports channel state but the dialog leaves the callback empty.
v2Gate: Control requires an open current data channel and helper input readiness.

name: helper_loss
currentOutcome: Per-WTS helper registry removal is reference-specific; the affected media route must recover independently.
v2Gate: One exact helper repair per child session; no cross-session fallback.

name: console_to_user_transition
currentOutcome: Historical workflow uses a fresh generation-1 user child after console login.
v2Gate: Keep console media until a selected exact user target is ready; no same-peer handover.
